Thank you. I've had a big problem with modern horror for quite some time. It's good to be able to put down exactly why

Well, you've certainly nailed it. I grew up with the old B&W horror classics and I love them. The directors did so much with so little, their use of light and shadow to create suspense and shock hasn't been matched yet. Well, maybe, but I haven't caught it.

The sequels thing is the copy machine effect applied to creativity. The first Nightmare film was awesome. Remember that scene where Freddie's arms extended across the width of an alley? The things nightmares are made from. They should have let it stand alone as an example of what a new idea is.

Most of the 80s/90s horror seemed to me little more than an excuse to show bare nubile breasts in a location other than a porn theater.

Actors acted more during that era, at least to me. I think they had to, because the special effects wouldn't carry the story over the hump of a dead pan actor. Karloff's expressions in The Mummy were exquisite. You didn't need explanations to understand the emotions at play.

Famous Monsters of Filmland was my only must-have read for many years.
Have you seen Stoker by Park Chan Wok? He nailed what felt like vintage horror movie environment with an fairly interesting tale. I'd love to see him approach more horror.
I have not. I will now, though. The wiki is kind of a spoiler, but it sounds pretty good. Thanks!

I love the horror genre, but its hung me out to dry. I go to all these new horror movies and don't get scared at all. I've seen so many of them that I usually know when the jump scare is going to happen, so it has no effect. I want movies to creep me out, like you said in your post. I completely agree with you 10/10.

Side note: a recent horror movie that I really enjoyed was the The Babadook. Creepy throughout the entire movie.

I personally have given up on the genre and won't see a horror movie unless I'm told it's actually good. Last one I really enjoyed was Let Me In and that's about 5 years old now. Although I here It Follows is good so I'll probably check that one out

I appreciate this. The horror genre shouldn't be only cheap scare but an interesting variety ranging from the aforementioned cheap scare to psychological near-torture.

And I hate jump scares. I tolerate a few ones in a well-made movie, but generally hate the shit out of them. It's not even scary, it's just biological reaction. It tricks us into thinking that we might be scared for a split-second, and then we just feel bad for falling for it. Good horror movies will be able to let the uneasiness linger with the viewer for hours. We don't have to see every bit of the monster, or every piece of extracted anatomy. An horror movie is, basically, like a suspense movie, but going further.

Is this so hard to understand that we cannot have more than maybe one good horror movie per year?

Spielberg in the director's cut of Jaws and the extended opening sequence nailed it, for a few minutes I could experience the terror and horror awaiting the victim and just be scared. No one really makes the effort to do that any more. The last good one I saw was probably The Grudge, maybe just me on that one.
